transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya + Ethan (Redwood SEs); Tom (Bluewater CTO), Priya (Head Infra), Liam (Security), Sara (DevOps)

Summary (auto-gen, imperfect): initial discovery for Private deployment / VPC options. Customer evaluating Dedicated vs Private, concerned about VPC peering, PrivateLink, cross-region endpoints, and control plane connectivity.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'll kick off — we invited Maya and Ethan to cover the network bits, cause we know Private deployments always have the tricky bits with VPCs and routing. quick run through agenda: high level requirements, current infra, network constraints, security/compliance, next steps.

[00:28] Tom: yeah thanks Jordan. we run most infra in us-east-1, small footprint in eu-west-1 for backups. main ask is we want redwood to run in our VPCs, no egress to public internet for inference traffic, and all keys stay in our KMS. timeline is Q2 pilot, production later in H2.

[00:46] Maya: got it. so private can be done two main ways typically: VPC peering (cross-account peering) or AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints). peering is simpler for low-latency but you have to manage route tables and overlapping CIDR; PrivateLink is more controlled and doesn't require routes, but introduces interface endpoints and ENIs in your subnet.

[01:10] Priya: we're using a /16 for our main VPC, and some child services use /20s in different accounts via Transit Gateway. we also use TGW for cross-region via attachments, so we need to know if redwood supports TGW peering or whether we need separate peering into the account.

[01:33] Ethan: quick note — Redwood Private supports both patterns. for customers who want full network isolation we often recommend establishing VPC peering or TGW attachments to our dedicated hosting VPC, but for stricter control and audit boundaries, PrivateLink (interface endpoint) is common. there's a tradeoff: peering allows direct 10s of ms latency, PrivateLink adds a small hop but isolates route tables.

[02:05] Liam: security question — does the control plane require outbound connectivity to redwood-managed control plane? we need to know whether the control plane sits in your cloud and if so, what endpoints we must allow; or can we host control plane privately?

[02:22] Jordan: good question. for our hosted private offering we offer a customer-managed control plane option that can be run in your VPC — but the standard pattern is a private control plane with optional peered control plane to Redwood for updates and telemetry. if you need air-gapped we do an on-prem package; otherwise we can arrange for control plane traffic over PrivateLink to our service endpoints. we'll put specifics in the security doc.

[02:47] Sara: how about egress for model downloads and occasional updates — that would need S3 access right? do we need NAT or can redwood push through via interface endpoint to our S3?

[03:05] Maya: model artifacts can be pulled from your S3 via role-based access if you prefer; typically we recommend using an S3 VPC endpoint (gateway endpoint) so no NAT required. Alternatively, if the models are hosted by Redwood, we can pull over PrivateLink to our artifact store but for customer-hosted artifacts you'd provide an IAM role or presigned urls.

[03:28] Tom: our security team is picky — KMS keys must never leave account, HSM-backed keys required for prod. can Redwood integrate with customer KMS/HSM for encryption at rest and TLS client certs?

[03:44] Ethan: yes, we support customer-managed KMS for data at rest in Private deployments; for HSM we have integrations depending on provider (AWS CloudHSM). we will capture exact key handling in the security whitepaper. TLS mutual auth is supported on PrivateLink endpoints if you need mTLS.

[04:05] Priya: IP addressing — overlapping CIDR is a no-go for us. if Redwood's managed VPC overlaps with our ranges it will be a blocker. can you confirm non-overlap requirement and the process?

[04:22] Maya: absolutely. for peering we require non-overlapping CIDRs. as part of onboarding we'll collect your CIDR blocks and propose ranges for the Redwood side; if you use TGW we can attach our VPC to your TGW — that helps centralize routing but you still must allow routes and security groups. we'll ask for a net diagram.

[04:47] Liam: audit logging — do you ship logs back to our S3 or CloudWatch? retention policies? we need immutable logs for 1 year and integration with our SIEM.

[05:02] Jordan: audit logs can be forwarded to your S3 or CloudWatch via our log-export mechanism; retention policies controlled by you. we also integrate with syslog/Splunk via forwarders. will include sample config in docs.

[05:20] Tom: latency expectations — for our use-case (real-time ETA predictions) tail latency needs to be < 150ms 95th percentile for single token, and throughput bursts of 200 qps. how does Redwood sizing look for that?

[05:38] Ethan: that'll depend on model size and quantization. for the reference models we typically see 50–100ms p95 for smaller models on Dedicated GPUs; Private deployments on same GPU types will match. we can run a short benchmark using your prompt patterns; recommend a 2-week pilot with a dedicated pool to validate p95 and scaling.

[06:02] Priya: any region constraints? we have data residency in eu-west and for production we want inference to stay in eu-west-1. can Redwood Private be deployed in eu-west-1?

[06:13] Maya: yes, we support customer deployments in major regions including eu-west-1 and us-east-1; for private we can provision the stack in your region. some specialized instance types might have limited availability — we will call that out. if you need multi-region failover we can discuss cross-region replication and warm standby.

[06:36] Tom: what about IAM — does Redwood require creating cross-account roles? how do you authenticate inbound traffic from our VPC?

[06:48] Ethan: typical pattern is we ask you to create an IAM role in your account that grants read-only access to the S3 buckets for artifacts and allow our managed principals to assume it for model pulls; network ingress is via peering or PrivateLink so we don't open public endpoints. for management APIs we can set up cross-account roles or federated access via SAML if you want.

[07:12] Jordan: quick note on costs: Dedicated vs Private — Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood-managed accounts; Private (VPC) has additional infra/setup costs for private control plane and networking. we'll include a pricing comparison and a pilot option in the follow-up.

[07:29] Priya: ok good. next steps from our side: we'll gather CIDR lists, TGW topology, and security requirements. also we'll loop in the network engineer (name forthcoming).

[07:40] Jordan: great. Maya, Ethan, any other items to call out?

[07:45] Maya: just that we'll prepare a matrix of connectivity options (peering vs PrivateLink vs TGW) with pros/cons and sample route table changes. also include examples for S3 VPC endpoints and KMS policies.

[07:58] Ethan: I'll add a note about model pull flows and required IAM policies plus example CloudFormation snippets.

[08:06] Tom: perfect. also include timeline options — 2-week pilot, 3-month pilot, and what success metrics we should define (latency p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens).

[08:22] Jordan: noted. we'll send the security doc and architecture diagram by Friday. want to pick a follow-up deep-dive for next week to go into network-level details and maybe run a quick connectivity test.

[08:34] Priya: Tue works for us (2026-03-31) morning ET.

[08:40] Jordan: ok we'll send invites after the call. thanks all.

Recap (auto): Action items — Jordan to send security docs; Maya to schedule deep-dive; customer to share VPC/CIDR/TGW info. Follow-up deep-dive tentatively 2026-03-31.

References mentioned: link to Redwood Private deployment overview (shared in chat), sample security whitepaper (to be sent), example CloudFormation snippets (Ethan will share).

End of transcript.
